solution:
Area \(= \frac{1}{2}\left| \begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right|\) with vertices \((1, 0), (6, 0), (4, 3)\).
\(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 6 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 1(0 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3) - 0(6 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 4) + 1(6 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 4)\)
\(= 1(-3) - 0 + 1(18) = -3 + 18 = 15\).
Area \(= \frac{1}{2}|15| = \frac{15}{2}\) sq. units.

The points are collinear if the area of the triangle they form is zero, i.e. the determinant of the coordinate matrix is \(0\).
\(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a & b + c & 1 \\ b & c + a & 1 \\ c & a + b & 1 \end{vmatrix}\).
Apply \(C_2 \to C_2 + C_1\):
\(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a & a + b + c & 1 \\ b & a + b + c & 1 \\ c & a + b + c & 1 \end{vmatrix}\).
Take the common factor \((a + b + c)\) out of \(C_2\):
\(\Delta = (a + b + c) \begin{vmatrix} a & 1 & 1 \\ b & 1 & 1 \\ c & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\).
Columns \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) are identical, so the determinant is \(0\). Hence \(\Delta = 0\) and the points \(A, B, C\) are collinear.

The equation of the line through \((1, 2)\) and \((3, 6)\) is obtained by setting the area determinant of a general point \((x, y)\) with the two points to zero:
\(\begin{vmatrix} x & y & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).
Expanding along \(R_1\):
\(x(2 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 6) - y(1 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3) + 1(1 \cdot 6 - 2 \cdot 3) = 0\)
\(x(-4) - y(-2) + (6 - 6) = 0 \Rightarrow -4x + 2y = 0\).
Dividing by \(2\): \(y = 2x\).

The equation of the line through \((3, 1)\) and \((9, 3)\) is given by:
\(\begin{vmatrix} x & y & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).
Expanding along \(R_1\):
\(x(1 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3) - y(3 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 9) + 1(3 \cdot 3 - 1 \cdot 9) = 0\)
\(x(-2) - y(-6) + (9 - 9) = 0 \Rightarrow -2x + 6y = 0\).
Dividing by \(-2\): \(x - 3y = 0\).

The system is \(x + 2y = 2\), \(2x + 3y = 3\), i.e. \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1 \cdot 3 - 2 \cdot 2 = 3 - 4 = -1 \neq 0\).
Since \(|A| \neq 0\), \(A\) is non-singular, so \(A^{-1}\) exists and the system has a unique solution. Hence the system is consistent.

The system is \(2x - y = 5\), \(x + y = 4\), i.e. \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2 \cdot 1 - (-1) \cdot 1 = 2 + 1 = 3 \neq 0\).
Since \(|A| \neq 0\), \(A\) is non-singular and the system has a unique solution. Hence the system is consistent.

The system is \(x + 3y = 5\), \(2x + 6y = 8\), i.e. \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1 \cdot 6 - 3 \cdot 2 = 6 - 6 = 0\).
Since \(|A| = 0\), compute \((\operatorname{adj} A) B\). Here \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\operatorname{adj} A) B = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 30 - 24 \\ -10 + 8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \neq O\).
Since \(|A| = 0\) and \((\operatorname{adj} A) B \neq O\), the system is inconsistent (has no solution).

The system is \(x + y + z = 1\), \(2x + 3y + 2z = 2\), \(ax + ay + 2az = 4\), with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ a & a & 2a \end{bmatrix}\).
Taking \(a\) common from \(R_3\): \(|A| = a \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\).
\(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 1(3 \cdot 2 - 2 \cdot 1) - 1(2 \cdot 2 - 2 \cdot 1) + 1(2 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot 1) = 1(4) - 1(2) + 1(-1) = 1\).
So \(|A| = a\). For \(a \neq 0\), \(|A| \neq 0\), so \(A\) is non-singular and the system has a unique solution. Hence the system is consistent.

The system is \(3x - y - 2z = 2\), \(2y - z = -1\), \(3x - 5y = 3\), with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 3(2 \cdot 0 - (-1)(-5)) - (-1)(0 \cdot 0 - (-1) \cdot 3) + (-2)(0 \cdot (-5) - 2 \cdot 3)\)
\(= 3(-5) + 1(3) - 2(-6) = -15 + 3 + 12 = 0\).
Since \(|A| = 0\), compute \((\operatorname{adj} A) B\). The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} -5 & -3 & -6 \\ 10 & 6 & 12 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 10 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 3 \\ -6 & 12 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\operatorname{adj} A) B = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 10 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 3 \\ -6 & 12 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -10 - 10 + 15 \\ -6 - 6 + 9 \\ -12 - 12 + 18 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -9 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix} \neq O\).
Since \(|A| = 0\) and \((\operatorname{adj} A) B \neq O\), the system is inconsistent.

The system is \(5x - y + 4z = 5\), \(2x + 3y + 5z = 2\), \(5x - 2y + 6z = -1\), with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 5 & -2 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 5(3 \cdot 6 - 5 \cdot (-2)) - (-1)(2 \cdot 6 - 5 \cdot 5) + 4(2 \cdot (-2) - 3 \cdot 5)\)
\(= 5(18 + 10) + 1(12 - 25) + 4(-4 - 15) = 5(28) + (-13) + 4(-19) = 140 - 13 - 76 = 51 \neq 0\).
Since \(|A| \neq 0\), \(A\) is non-singular and the system has a unique solution. Hence the system is consistent.

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 7 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 5 \cdot 3 - 2 \cdot 7 = 15 - 14 = 1 \neq 0\).
\(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|} \operatorname{adj} A = \frac{1}{1} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 12 - 10 \\ -28 + 25 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 2\), \(y = -3\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2 \cdot 4 - (-1) \cdot 3 = 8 + 3 = 11 \neq 0\).
\(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{11} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{11} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{11} \begin{bmatrix} -8 + 3 \\ 6 + 6 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{11} \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = -\frac{5}{11}\), \(y = \frac{12}{11}\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 4 \cdot (-5) - (-3) \cdot 3 = -20 + 9 = -11 \neq 0\).
\(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{-11} \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 3 \\ -3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{-11} \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 3 \\ -3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{-11} \begin{bmatrix} -15 + 21 \\ -9 + 28 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{-11} \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 19 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = -\frac{6}{11}\), \(y = -\frac{19}{11}\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 5 \cdot 2 - 2 \cdot 3 = 10 - 6 = 4 \neq 0\).
\(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -3 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 6 - 10 \\ -9 + 25 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 16 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = -1\), \(y = 4\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 9 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2((-2)(-5) - (-1)(3)) - 1((1)(-5) - (-1)(0)) + 1((1)(3) - (-2)(0)) = 2(13) - 1(-5) + 1(3) = 34\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 13 & 5 & 3 \\ 8 & -10 & -6 \\ 1 & 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 8 & 1 \\ 5 & -10 & 3 \\ 3 & -6 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{34} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{34} \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 8 & 1 \\ 5 & -10 & 3 \\ 3 & -6 & -5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{34} \begin{bmatrix} 13 + 12 + 9 \\ 5 - 15 + 27 \\ 3 - 9 - 45 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{34} \begin{bmatrix} 34 \\ 17 \\ -51 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 1\), \(y = \frac{1}{2}\), \(z = -\frac{3}{2}\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1(1 \cdot 1 - (-3)(1)) - (-1)(2 \cdot 1 - (-3)(1)) + 1(2 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 1) = 1(4) + 1(5) + 1(1) = 10\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 2 \\ -5 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{10} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 2 \\ -5 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 16 + 0 + 4 \\ -20 + 0 + 10 \\ 4 - 0 + 6 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 20 \\ -10 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 2\), \(y = -1\), \(z = 1\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2((-2)(-2) - (1)(-1)) - 3((1)(-2) - (1)(3)) + 3((1)(-1) - (-2)(3)) = 2(5) - 3(-5) + 3(5) = 40\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 5 & 5 \\ 3 & -13 & 11 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 3 & 9 \\ 5 & -13 & 1 \\ 5 & 11 & -7 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{40} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{40} \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 3 & 9 \\ 5 & -13 & 1 \\ 5 & 11 & -7 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{40} \begin{bmatrix} 25 - 12 + 27 \\ 25 + 52 + 3 \\ 25 - 44 - 21 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{40} \begin{bmatrix} 40 \\ 80 \\ -40 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 1\), \(y = 2\), \(z = -1\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ -5 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1(4 \cdot 3 - (-5)(-1)) - (-1)(3 \cdot 3 - (-5)(2)) + 2(3 \cdot (-1) - 4 \cdot 2) = 1(7) + 1(19) + 2(-11) = 4\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 7 & -19 & -11 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -3 & 11 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 1 & -3 \\ -19 & -1 & 11 \\ -11 & -1 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{4} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 1 & -3 \\ -19 & -1 & 11 \\ -11 & -1 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ -5 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 49 - 5 - 36 \\ -133 + 5 + 132 \\ -77 + 5 + 84 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 4 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 2\), \(y = 1\), \(z = 3\).

Given \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2(2 \cdot (-2) - (-4)(1)) - (-3)(3 \cdot (-2) - (-4)(1)) + 5(3 \cdot 1 - 2 \cdot 1) = 2(0) + 3(-2) + 5(1) = -1\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -9 & -5 \\ 2 & 23 & 13 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -9 & 23 \\ 1 & -5 & 13 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|} \operatorname{adj} A = \frac{1}{-1} \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -9 & 23 \\ 1 & -5 & 13 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 9 & -23 \\ -1 & 5 & -13 \end{bmatrix}\).
The system \(2x - 3y + 5z = 11\), \(3x + 2y - 4z = -5\), \(x + y - 2z = -3\) is \(AX = B\) with \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 11 \\ -5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 9 & -23 \\ -1 & 5 & -13 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 11 \\ -5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 - 5 + 6 \\ -22 - 45 + 69 \\ -11 - 25 + 39 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 1\), \(y = 2\), \(z = 3\).

Let the cost per kg of onion, wheat and rice be \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) rupees. The data give:
\(4x + 3y + 2z = 60\), \(2x + 4y + 6z = 90\), \(6x + 2y + 3z = 70\).
Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 90 \\ 70 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 4(4 \cdot 3 - 6 \cdot 2) - 3(2 \cdot 3 - 6 \cdot 6) + 2(2 \cdot 2 - 4 \cdot 6) = 4(0) - 3(-30) + 2(-20) = 50\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 30 & -20 \\ -5 & 0 & 10 \\ 10 & -20 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 30 & 0 & -20 \\ -20 & 10 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{50} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{50} \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 30 & 0 & -20 \\ -20 & 10 & 10 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 90 \\ 70 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{50} \begin{bmatrix} 0 - 450 + 700 \\ 1800 + 0 - 1400 \\ -1200 + 900 + 700 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{50} \begin{bmatrix} 250 \\ 400 \\ 400 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(x = 5\), \(y = 8\), \(z = 8\). The cost is: onion Rs 5 per kg, wheat Rs 8 per kg, and rice Rs 8 per kg.

Put \(u = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(v = \dfrac{1}{y}\), \(w = \dfrac{1}{z}\). The system becomes linear:
\(2u + 3v + 10w = 4\), \(4u - 6v + 5w = 1\), \(6u + 9v - 20w = 2\).
Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 10 \\ 4 & -6 & 5 \\ 6 & 9 & -20 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 2((-6)(-20) - 5 \cdot 9) - 3(4 \cdot (-20) - 5 \cdot 6) + 10(4 \cdot 9 - (-6)(6)) = 2(75) - 3(-110) + 10(72) = 1200\).
The cofactor matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 75 & 110 & 72 \\ 150 & -100 & 0 \\ 75 & 30 & -24 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 75 & 150 & 75 \\ 110 & -100 & 30 \\ 72 & 0 & -24 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{1200} \operatorname{adj} A\).
\(X = A^{-1} B = \frac{1}{1200} \begin{bmatrix} 75 & 150 & 75 \\ 110 & -100 & 30 \\ 72 & 0 & -24 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{1200} \begin{bmatrix} 300 + 150 + 150 \\ 440 - 100 + 60 \\ 288 + 0 - 48 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{1200} \begin{bmatrix} 600 \\ 400 \\ 240 \end{bmatrix}\).
So \(u = \frac{1}{2}\), \(v = \frac{1}{3}\), \(w = \frac{1}{5}\). Therefore \(x = \frac{1}{u} = 2\), \(y = \frac{1}{v} = 3\), \(z = \frac{1}{w} = 5\).
